evals.prompt: Create a 2-page Metis branded PDF called 'MECE_Framework_Overview.pdf' and save it to C:/temp/metis-pdf-test/. Page 1 should be a dark blue cover with the title 'MECE Framework' and subtitle 'A structured approach to problem-solving'. Page 2 should have a section header 'What is MECE?', a short paragraph explaining the concept, and a callout box titled 'Why it matters' with 2-3 sentences. Use Metis brand standards throughout.
evals.expected_output: A 2-page PDF at C:/temp/metis-pdf-test/MECE_Framework_Overview.pdf with a dark blue cover page featuring the trajectory fan device and correct brand colors, and a content page with page furniture, section header with SnglArrow accent, body paragraph, and a teal callout box. No text overlap. BrandLine in footer.

assertions.name: file_exists
assertions.description: PDF file was created at the specified path

assertions.name: minimum_file_size
assertions.description: PDF is at least 5KB (rules out empty/corrupt file)

assertions.name: uses_pdfkit
assertions.description: Script uses pdfkit (not a different PDF library)

assertions.name: uses_brand_colors
assertions.description: Script contains Metis dark blue hex code

assertions.name: uses_brandline
assertions.description: Script contains the exact BrandLine text

assertions.name: uses_explicit_y
assertions.description: Script uses explicit y coordinates in text calls (not relying on flow)

evals.prompt: Build me a 3-page Metis internal guide PDF titled 'AI Tools Quick Reference' — save it to C:/temp/metis-pdf-test/AI_Tools_Quick_Reference.pdf. Cover page (dark blue, branded). Page 2: section called 'Core Tools' with 4 step-style items (numbered 1-4) explaining Claude Code, Tessl, GitHub, and the skill-creator tile. Page 3: section called 'When to Use What' with a Nexus device divider, then 3 role/feature cards showing use cases for junior consultants, senior consultants, and project leads. End page 3 with a dark blue closing callout.
evals.expected_output: A 3-page PDF with branded cover, step rows on page 2, Nexus divider and role cards on page 3. Content should not overlap. All Metis brand elements applied. Graphic devices used appropriately.

assertions.name: file_exists
assertions.description: PDF file was created at the specified path

assertions.name: minimum_file_size
assertions.description: PDF is at least 8KB (3 pages with graphics)

assertions.name: uses_step_row_pattern
assertions.description: Script defines or uses a step row pattern

assertions.name: uses_nexus_device
assertions.description: Script references the Nexus graphic device

evals.prompt: I need a quick 1-page Metis one-pager PDF (cover page only, no additional pages) for a leadership update about our Context as Code initiative. Save it to C:/temp/metis-pdf-test/CaC_Leadership_Update.pdf. It should have the dark blue cover style with: a title 'Context as Code', subtitle 'Quarterly initiative update', a 'What we built' section listing 3 accomplishments as bullets, a 'What comes next' section with 2 bullets, and the standard Metis footer. Make it feel polished and leadership-ready.
evals.expected_output: A single-page PDF with dark blue background, trajectory fan device, bold title and subtitle, two labeled sections with bullet points, green divider lines, and branded footer with BrandLine. Professional and leadership-appropriate.

assertions.name: file_exists
assertions.description: PDF file was created at the specified path

assertions.name: single_page
assertions.description: Script does not call addPage (single page document)

assertions.name: uses_trajectory_fan
assertions.description: Script uses drawn trajectory fan (opacity-based triangles) for cover
